reason: The text contains only three named individual characters who participate in the narrative: (1) Jonah (יוֹנָה), a prophet sent by God, who possesses spiritual authority; (2) God/The Lord (יְהוָה), the supreme divine authority; and (3) the King of Nineveh (מֶלֶךְ נִֽינְוֵה), a political ruler. All other figures mentioned—sailors, the ship's captain, and the people of Nineveh—are referred to only by their collective roles and are never individually named. Each of the three named characters exercises leadership authority within the narrative: Jonah as a prophet delivering God's message, God as the commanding divine authority, and the King as the political leader of Nineveh.
